Title: Heavy rain brings relief as Johor haze readings remain moderate
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Heavy rain across parts of Johor this evening brought some relief from the haze, with air quality readings at all eight monitoring stations remaining at moderate levels.
As of this evening, Larkin recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 96, followed by Tangkak (92), Pasir Gudang (88) and Batu Pahat (87).
The other readings were Kota Tinggi (83), Segamat (80), Kluang (80) and Pengerang (75).
The Environment Department's monitoring stations identified fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres (PM2.5) as the dominant pollutant at all eight locations.
An API reading of between 51 and 100 is classified as moderate, while readings above 100 indicate unhealthy air quality.
The heavy rain is expected to help disperse pollutants and improve air quality in the affected areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Istana Negri Sembilan draws media attention amid royal crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Members of the media have gathered outside the Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here since 2pm today ahead of an expected audience involving top leaders.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim are understood to be seeking an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, who is currently at the palace.
Several police vehicles were seen entering the palace compound as of 5pm, though no official executive vehicles have arrived yet.
The palace crisis in Negri Sembilan has been ongoing since April, when the Undang Yang Empat proclaimed the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
The Undang Yang Empat subsequently proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
Earlier today, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all state executive council (exco) members with
immediate effect.
According to a statement issued by Istana Negri Sembilan Grand Chamberlain Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, the decision was made after all affected exco members were found to have breached their oaths of office.
He said under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959, a member of the executive council holds office at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
However, Ismail claimed that terminating or revoking an exco member's appointment without the advice or request of the menteri besar was
legally erroneous, unconstitutional and of no legal effect.
In a statement issued today, Ismail claimed he was never consulted nor had he at any time advised the revocation of any Negri Sembilan exco member under Article 38(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AfD predicts Merz's exit as German chancellor faces mounting pressure
Article:
BERLIN: Germany's far-right AfD predicted Monday that Chancellor Friedrich Merz will be out of office before the end of the year, a day after his centre-right CDU party suffered two bruising state election defeats.
The Alternative for Germany came first in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania where the CDU sank to 4.9 per cent, below the threshold to stay in parliament and its worst result since the party was formed in 1945.
"The chancellor certainly won't make it to the end of the year," said Leif-Erik Holm, the AfD's top candidate in the Baltic Sea coastal state. "I think the twilight of the chancellor's era has begun."
At just 16 months in office, Merz has seen his approval ratings plummet while his party has suffered a string of state vote losses against the AfD, which also leads the nationwide polls.
Fighting speculation that his CDU/CSU bloc may try to oust him, the 70-year-old chancellor took the unusual step of addressing the nation on TV on Sunday, just minutes after the first exit polls were announced.
Merz admitted that his CDU had suffered a "disaster" in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
While the AfD came first there, the centre-left SPD party looks set to continue governing the state if it can form a coalition with left-wing allies.
- RESIGNATION ON THE CARDS? -
After the CDU was also soundly defeated by a far-left Die Linke in Berlin, Merz charged that "trust in our country's institutions is waning" and being "actively undermined by radical parties on both the left and the right."
"What needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness and patience," Merz said. "I will demonstrate this as CDU party chairman and, above all, as chancellor of our country."
Analysts saw it as an attempt to gain the advantage before another hailstorm of criticism.
"His extremely early move shows that Merz is staking a claim to define the narrative," political scientist Oliver Lembcke of Ruhr University Bochum told AFP.
Lembcke labelled this "leadership from a defensive position – and an attempt to prevent a personnel debate with an uncertain outcome from gathering steam."
ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said of Merz's unusual TV address: "Read the appearance for what it was, an attempt to choke off the speculation about his possible resignation that has been building in recent weeks."
- TOUGH WEEK AHEAD -
The chancellor has also cleared his calendar for the following days and skipped a trip to New York for the UN General Assembly to deal with potential aftershocks from the votes.
Merz has been fighting off rumours he may be ousted for weeks.
Names of hopefuls for the top job that have been floated include Hendrik Wuest, state premier of populous North Rhine-Westphalia, and Markus Soeder, the Bavarian state premier and head of the CSU, the regional sister party of the CDU.
However, no contender has made an open move for the job – perhaps fearing the act of disloyalty could backfire, or intimidated by the tough task of trying to revive the party's fortunes during one of its worst-ever crises.
When Merz took office in May last year, he vowed to reboot a flagging economy, rebuild the military to deter Russia and reduce irregular immigration to soothe voters' fears and lure them away from the AfD.
But his personal approval ratings are hovering just above 10 per cent, not helped by his occasionally blunt and abrasive comments.
The latest elections came two weeks after the far-right, pro-Trump and Moscow-friendly AfD also dealt a stunning defeat to the CDU in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.
The string of election debacles comes as Merz has struggled to push through promised economic and social welfare reforms with his coalition partners in the SPD.
Under-fire Merz received some badly needed support from CDU powerbrokers last week when eight state premiers declared jointly that Germany needs "stability now more than ever" rather than "discussions about personnel."
They refrained, however, from issuing a personal endorsement of the chancellor.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP ministers, deputies staying in Cabinet at Loke's request
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision by DAP ministers and deputy ministers to remain in the Cabinet was made at the request of the party's secretary-general, Anthony Loke.
A source said all DAP ministers and deputy ministers had initially wanted to follow Loke's move to offer their resignation.
"However, the DAP central executive committee (CEC), particularly Loke, asked all the ministers and deputy ministers to remain in the government administration.
"This is because Loke did not want the government to collapse as a result of their withdrawal from the Cabinet," the source said when contacted.
Loke
had resigned as Transport Minister
following the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
Loke announced his decision after a three-hour CEC meeting to discuss the party's stance on Najib's conditional house arrest.
Loke said his decision to step down was a personal stance, while the other ministers would remain in their positions to maintain political stability.
"If all DAP ministers were to resign, the government could collapse, leading to political instability, which is precisely what our opponents are waiting for.
"DAP would not allow opposition forces to exploit the situation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy rain five times usual level triggered KL flash floods
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas.
Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital.
"Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.
"As of 5.30pm, Lembah Keramat recorded the highest accumulated rainfall at 155.5 mm, compared with the usual 30 mm," he said during a press conference here today.
According to media reports, heavy rain that swept across the federal capital on Sunday afternoon resulted in flooding in several areas, including Ampang, Taman U-Thant and Jalan Ampang, disrupting traffic.
Meanwhile, on the issue of foreign worker accommodation at the Federal Territory Affordable Housing Project (Residensi Max) on Jalan Kolam Air, Fadlun said the Commissioner of Buildings (COB) had warned the project developer against converting utility rooms into housing for foreign workers.
"Residensi Max remains under the developer's supervision. Therefore, the COB has issued a warning letter to the developer, reminding the developer not to house workers in areas or rooms designated for other purposes, and we will continue to monitor the situation," he said.
The media had previously reported concerns among Residensi Max residents over the presence of foreigners at the residence, with the situation allegedly having persisted for nearly a year.
Residensi Max Residents' Association chairman Muhammed Assyafiq Ahmad Kamal reportedly expressed frustration with the management, alleging that it had refused to cooperate with residents to resolve the issue.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka lawmakers await 'whistle' for assembly dissolution
Article:
MELAKA: The dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly is expected to take place this week, based on an earlier indication by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem said the "two Fridays" referred to by the chief minister had already arrived.
"If we go by the signal given by the Melaka chief minister about the two Fridays to go before the state assembly dissolution, those two Fridays have already passed.
"So, for us assemblymen, we have not just been working for the election. We have been working since the last election ended," he said when contacted today.
Helmy, who is also Melaka deputy executive councillor for Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications, said the decision on whom to elect would be left entirely to the people.
Meanwhile, Kota Laksamana assemblyman Low Chee Leong said he was also ready and was now only waiting for the "whistle" for the dissolution.
"I'm ready, just waiting for the whistle. I have been working on the ground every day since polling day of the 2021 Melaka state election.
"I am always prepared, just as I am when attending state assembly sittings, ready to speak and ask questions at any time," said the DAP representative.
Media reports previously quoted Rauf as saying the Melaka state assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman had said the dissolution would take place in
"two more Fridays".
Earlier, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was reported to have urged Rauf to expedite the dissolution announcement to pave the way for the state election.
He reportedly said the announcement should not be delayed too long as the people, particularly youths, should be given the opportunity to determine the direction and future of the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ensure polytechnic, community college grads secure jobs matching their skills - Zambry
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The employability rate of polytechnics and community colleges (PolyCC) should be viewed beyond mere percentage figures, ensuring graduates secure jobs that match their skills and offer quality career prospects and suitable income levels.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir reminded polytechnics and community colleges not to rest on their laurels despite their graduates recording employability rates exceeding 98 per cent last year.
"What is more important is to ensure graduates secure jobs that match their skills, have good career prospects and offer good income. That is why the relationship between educational institutions and the industry must evolve further.
"Industry needs to work with us from the curriculum development, training and certification stages through to employment opportunities," he said in his speech at the 2026 Sabah Zone Polytechnic and Community College Convocation Ceremony at Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic today.
He said rapid technological advances in artificial intelligence (AI), automation, robotics, green technology, cybersecurity and digital economy have also altered the employment landscape and the skills required by the industry.
In this rapidly evolving professional landscape, Zambry said the nation needs graduates who are not only knowledgeable but also capable of solving problems, mastering technology, thinking creatively and staying adaptable to change.
He said Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) is no longer a second choice, but has instead become one of the main career pathways for the country's younger generation, since the TVET 2.0 Agenda emphasises high-demand future sectors such as AI, robotics and renewable energy.
As such, Zambry said the Ministry of Higher Education has made "PolyCC as the TVET Pioneer" one of the thrusts of the country's higher education sector, reinforced by the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 and the Polytechnic and Community College Strategic Plan 2026-2035.
He said the PolyCC ecosystem currently encompasses 36 polytechnics and 106 community colleges nationwide, with over 100,000 students.
He also said that, in Sabah, the three polytechnics and nine community colleges played an important role in providing access to education and developing local talent in the state.
Zambry added that the TVET development agenda in Sabah is crucial to supporting the growth of the state's economic sectors, including energy, oil and gas, tourism, modern agriculture, construction, the digital economy, logistics and the blue economy.
"Sabah's economic development must move in tandem with the development of local talent. As such, we want more Sabah youths to obtain quality education, master high-level skills and subsequently secure good employment opportunities," he said.
Meanwhile, Zambry told reporters that five more polytechnics would soon offer degree-level study programmes as part of efforts to expand higher education pathways in technical and engineering fields.
So far, he said four polytechnics already offer degree-level study programmes in those fields.
This approach, he said, was important to meet the country's workforce requirements, while ensuring polytechnic education remains aligned with industry demands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia condemns  repeated incursions at Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first kiblat and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended.
"History proves that barbaric incursions into al-Aqsa have always been the catalyst for a wave of awakening among the ummah.
"The Zionist regime cannot be allowed to normalise these extremist actions, which risk pushing the world into a more complex global conflict," he said in a statement today.
In light of this, Zulkifli urged the international community to take immediate and firm action against the Zionist regime, rather than merely issuing rhetorical condemnations.
He also called on Muslims in the country to continue uniting in solidarity and performing the
qunut nazilah
prayer so that Allah SWT may preserve the sanctity of the Al-Aqsa Mosque and liberate Palestinian land from the grip of tyranny.
The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's daughter Putri Norlisa joins CTOS board
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd has appointed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's daughter Putri Norlisa Najib as an independent non-executive director.
The appointment of the 45-year-old lawyer will take effect on Sept 25, the credit reporting group said in Bursa Malaysia filings on Monday.
Putri Norlisa is the daughter of Najib and his former wife Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar.
She is currently joint managing partner of law firm Adnan Sundra & Low and has more than 20 years of legal experience, particularly in banking and finance.
According to CTOS, Putri Norlisa began her legal career in 2005 at Eversheds in London, where she trained and practised as a solicitor specialising in banking.
She returned to Malaysia and was called to the Bar in 2009 before practising at Kadir, Andri & Partners, where she became a partner.
Putri Norlisa later co-founded Putri Norlisa Chair in 2015. The firm merged with Adnan Sundra & Low in 2018, where she became joint managing partner in 2023.
Her work covers local and cross-border banking and finance transactions, including project finance, debt restructuring and private debt securities.
She also advises on mergers and acquisitions, joint ventures, capital market transactions and regulatory requirements across various industries.
Putri Norlisa holds law degrees at bachelor's and master's levels from the University of Nottingham and is a member of the Malaysian Bar.
She will join CTOS' Risk and Compliance Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Employee Share Option Scheme Committee, also effective Sept 25.
CTOS said Putri Norlisa's only other directorship is with charitable organisation Noah Foundation, where she serves as an alternate director.
Meanwhile, the group also appointed Chan Siew Mei of AMMB Holdings Bhd as an independent non-executive director effective Sept 25. She has held the same position at AMMB since June 2025 and chairs its Audit and Examination Committee.
Chan, 60, has 40 years of experience in audit, accounting, deals and consulting, including as head of advisory and chief financial officer of KPMG Malaysia.
She will also take over as chairman of CTOS' Audit Committee from Sept 25.
The two appointments follow the retirement of Nirmala Doraisamy as an independent non-executive director effective Sept 21.
CTOS said Nirmala had no disagreement with the board and there were no matters arising from her retirement that needed to be brought to shareholders' attention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former deputy rural development minister Yahya Lampong dies at 86
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Former deputy rural development minister and Kota Belud member of parliament Datuk Yahya Lampong died at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital in Kuala Lumpur around 6am.
He was 86.
His death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post. The cause of death has yet to be confirmed.
"May Allah forgive his sins, shower him with His mercy, and grant him Jannatul Firdaus. Please keep Papa in your doa," Masley said.
He said the remains were taken to Nurul Islam Mosque in Ampang for bathing and funeral prayers.
Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.
He also served as the Tempasuk state assemblyman on the United Sabah National Organisation ticket from 1985 to 1986.
Yahya began his political career in 1981 when he contested the Usukan state seat on the Parti Bersatu Rakyat Jelata Sabah (Berjaya) ticket.
He later contested the Papar parliamentary seat as a PKR candidate in the 2013 General Election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Janda Baik visitors advised to check with resorts after flash floods
Article:
BENTONG: Visitors planning to travel to Janda Baik are advised to contact their respective resorts, chalets or homestays before making the journey following yesterday's flash floods in Kampung Janda Baik.
A spokesman for the Janda Baik Resort Association said only four chalets and homestays operating along Sungai Cherangin were affected by the overflowing river, while the remaining premises were operating as usual.
"The floodwaters have receded and a major clean-up operation was carried out at the four affected premises today. There were no guests staying at the resorts when the flash floods occurred yesterday.
"Guests who have made bookings and plan to travel to Janda Baik are advised to contact their respective resorts, chalets or homestays. The floods did not affect the entire settlement," said the spokesman.
The spokesman also urged the public not to share unverified images or information about the floods on social media, saying this could cause unnecessary concern among those planning to travel to the area.
"Obtain first-hand information by contacting the respective resorts or chalets. The roads to Janda Baik are unaffected."
The floods occurred when Sungai Cherangin overflowed its banks following continuous heavy rain at about 4pm yesterday, sending swift-flowing, murky water into resort compounds and inundating parts of the premises.
The water receded quickly but left behind a large amount of debris.
A total of
105 people
from 34 families in Kampung Janda Baik were evacuated to SK Janda Baik after their homes were submerged.
Meanwhile, Bentong Civil Defence Force officer Azizah Husain said all 34 families evacuated to the relief centre at about 6pm yesterday had been allowed to return home.
She said the villagers returned to clean their homes earlier today before the relief centre was closed at 1.20pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Unhealthy air quality recorded in 17 areas as of 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 17 areas still recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, with Kapit in Sarawak the worst hit with a reading of 172.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Sarawak with unhealthy air quality were Serian IPD (167), Sibu (164), Sri Aman (163), Bintulu (160) and Samalaju (158).
Kuching (Sarawak) and Cheras (Kuala Lumpur) each recorded readings of 157, while Putrajaya and Nilai (Negri Sembilan) recorded 156.
Other areas with unhealthy API readings were Samarahan (155) and Miri (153) in Sarawak; Seremban (152) in Negri Sembilan; Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic (143) in Sabah; Johan Setia (133) and Shah Alam (123) in Selangor; and Sarikei (104) in Sarawak.
Meanwhile, 41 areas recorded moderate readings, while six areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous).

Title: 1MDB files leave to appeal ruling that High Court lacks jurisdiction to hear suit against UK law firm
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court's ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm.
Lawyer Lim Zhi Ying, one of the lawyers representing 1MDB, confirmed the notice of motion was filed on Aug 28, this year.
She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application.
In its application, 1MDB sought leave to appeal the Court of Appeal's decision, citing that there are important questions of general principles to be decided for the first time by the top court.
1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.
Among the questions include whether in determining the forum conveniens (an appropriate forum) for a claim in conspiracy involving alleged conspirators across multiple jurisdictions, the relevant connecting factors to be assessed by reference to the alleged conspiracy as a whole, including the places where the other alleged conspirators and material witnesses are located, and not by reference to the circumstances and location of the particular foreign defendant challenging jurisdiction.
On Aug 20, this year, a three-member bench comprising Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, allowed White and Case LLB's appeal, ruling that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB's suit against the firm.
Justice Muniandy, who delivered the unanimous decision, held that the requirements under the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 and the Rules of Court 2012 for the service of proceedings outside Malaysia had not been satisfied.
He said 1MDB failed to prove that Malaysia is clearly the forum convenient to hear this suit, adding that Patrick Mahony, a director of PetroSaudi International Ltd, is a foreign national residing outside Malaysia and therefore could not serve as a proper "anchor defendant" to justify the service of proceedings out of jurisdiction.
The panel also set aside the High Court's decision to consolidate 1MDB's suit against White & Case with a separate suit filed by the sovereign wealth fund against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
1MDB filed the suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US1.83 billion and US33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony.
The fund alleged that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
The alleged misconduct relates to two corporate transactions: the 2009 joint venture with PetroSaudi International, known as the Good Star phase, and the 2010 restructuring of 1MDB's stake in the joint venture, which 1MDB claims resulted in significant financial losses.
The writ of summons was served out of jurisdiction on White & Case at their UK offices, and the firm subsequently applied to set aside the service, seeking a declaration that the Malaysian court had no jurisdiction to hear the suit.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case's challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-sports ministry officer denied fair trial, High Court hears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Youth and Sports Ministry finance division secretary Otman Arsahd was denied a fair trial due to serious misdirection by the Sessions Court in evaluating prosecution evidence, the High Court heard.
His lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said the misdirection had resulted in a miscarriage of justice and rendered Otman's conviction on 32 charges of abuse of power and 64 money laundering counts unsafe.
He said the second Sessions Court judge had failed to fully evaluate the evidence before convicting Otman, 67, and sentencing him to 15 years in jail and fining him RM284.2 million in 2023.
Rafique said 70 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial, but the second judge personally heard only SP64 to SP70.
He said the judge had not personally heard the evidence of SP1 to SP63, who comprised about 90 per cent of the prosecution's witnesses.
He questioned whether the judge had the same audio-visual advantage in evaluating witness testimonies and determining whether a prima facie case had been established.
"The issue is not whether a judge is allowed to take over a case. We accept that it is permitted under the law.
"The issue is whether the second judge truly applied his mind to all the evidence previously recorded, particularly the evidence of the material prosecution witnesses and their cross-examination," he submitted.
Rafique said the grounds of judgment did not demonstrate that the judge had conducted a full evaluation of the prosecution's evidence, particularly the testimony of key witnesses SP27, SP29 and SP11.
He said this was critical in determining how the court had arrived at its prima facie finding against Otman.
"The judge failed to appreciate all the evidence before him. My client was not accorded a fair trial, which resulted in a serious misdirection and occasioned a miscarriage of justice.
"I ask that the appeal against his conviction and sentence is allowed," said Rafique during an appeal hearing set for three days before judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin.
Rafique also challenged the prosecution's decision to call Otman's second and third co-accused as SP64 and SP65 after they entered into plea-bargain agreements with the prosecution.
He argued that it was unfair to Otman for the two co-accused to become prosecution witnesses after spending about two years with him throughout the trial.
The two accused had sat together with him in the dock, shared the same defence strategy and cross-examination approach, and participated in discussions about the case, he said.
Rafique argued that the prosecution had already been exposed to the defence's strategy and narrative before the two men became prosecution witnesses.
"SP64 and SP65 should be viewed not simply as accomplices who turned witnesses, but as 'prosecution spies'," he submitted.
The prosecution is represented by deputy public prosecutors Haresh Prakash Somiah and Mohd Ashrof Adrin Kamarul.
The hearing continues tomorrow.
On July 6, 2023, judge Kamarudin Kamsun found Otman guilty on the 96 counts as he had failed to raise any reasonable doubt against the prosecution's case.
For the 17 offences involving false claims, the court ordered Otman to serve a cumulative prison sentence of 243 years and pay a fine of RM190 million, or in default, serve an additional 119 months in jail.
For the 15 charges of abuse of position, the accused was sentenced to a total of 85 years' jail and fined RM10.8 million, or in default, serve a further 125 months in jail.
Meanwhile, for the 64 charges of receiving proceeds from unlawful activities, the court ordered Otman to serve jail terms ranging from three months to 11 years and imposed a total fine of RM83.4 million, or in default, an additional 934 months' jail.
Kamarudin ordered all sentences to run concurrently from July 6, 2023, resulting in an effective jail term of 15 years.
Otman was allowed a stay of
execution of both the prison sentence and fine pending appeal, on condition that his bail be increased by RM300,000 with one surety. Previously, he had been released on bail of RM250,000 with one surety.
On April 21, 2016, Otman was charged with 64 counts of receiving RM16.623 million in proceeds from unlawful activities into accounts held with Maybank, RHB and CIMB Bank Bhd through cheques between March 7, 2012 and Dec 11, 2015.
The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
The offence carries a penalty of up to 15 years' jail, a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds of the unlawful activity, or both, upon conviction.

Title: Over 4,800 MRSM huffaz have entered professional fields to date - Asyraf
Article:
PARIT: Over 4,800 Quran memorisers (huffaz) produced by the Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) Ulul Albab programme have entered various professional sectors in Malaysia and abroad, says Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
He said the programme is on the right track, exceeding its Key Performance Indicator (KPI) target of producing at least 400 students who memorise all 30 chapters (juzuk) of the Quran each year.
"This year alone, we have exceeded our KPI, as 438 students completed memorising all 30 chapters of the Quran," he told reporters after closing the 2026 Deputy Prime Minister's Cup MRSM Debate competition at MRSM Parit here today.
Asyraf said the Ulul Albab Tamhidi or 'mini Ulul Albab' initiative, launched early last year, has now been expanded to all 50 MRSM campuses nationwide, in addition to the eight main MRSM Ulul Albab institutions.
He said the expansion enables students in other MRSMs to master at least five chapters of the Quran before completing Form Five, fulfilling the entry requirements for those wishing to pursue medical studies at Al-Azhar University in Cairo.
Meanwhile, MRSM Kuantan won the Malay Language category in the debate competition, defeating runners-up MRSM Pengkalan Hulu.
Opposing the motion to reinstate the mandatory death penalty, the team took home RM10,000 cash and a challenge trophy.
In the Arabic Language category, MRSM Gemencheh emerged champions after defeating MRSM Tun Ahmad Abdullah Badawi, while MRSM Langkawi won the English Language category by defeating MRSM Tun Ghafar Baba.
Held from Sept 18 to 21, this year's competition brought together 528 debaters from 58 MRSM campuses nationwide, with total cash prizes of RM53,000 on offer.
First introduced in 2009 and rebranded as the Deputy Prime Minister's Cup MRSM Debate competition in 2023, the tournament offers students as young as Form One the opportunity to debate alongside Form Five seniors in a healthy competitive environment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcyclist killed in three-vehicle crash at Sultan Iskandar Highway tunnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 22-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a three-vehicle accident at Tunnel 2 of the Sultan Iskandar Highway heading towards Jalan Damansara here this morning.
In the 9.50am incident, the victim, who was riding a Yamaha 135LC motorcycle, is believed to have lost control before crashing into the rear right side of a Honda City.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the victim was travelling in the right lane when he collided with the Honda City, which was in the same lane.
"Following the collision, the motorcyclist fell into the left lane before being hit by a lorry driven by a man.
"The lorry driver was unable to avoid the victim before hitting him," he said in a statement today.
He said the motorcyclist sustained serious injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant from Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
He said the two other drivers involved — a 28-year-old man driving the Honda City and a 40-year-old lorry driver — were unhurt.
Mohd Zamzuri urged members of the public or witnesses with information on the incident to come forward to assist investigations.
"They can contact the Tun H S Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.
"The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-China ties set for further boost during Anwar's China visit
Article:
SHANGHAI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's working visit to this metropolitan city, starting tomorrow in conjunction with WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, is significant in maintaining the momentum of close ties between Malaysia and China.
Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit reflects the growing bilateral relations, particularly following several official visits by China's top leadership over the past three years.
He said high-level exchanges during this period, involving the prime minister, deputy prime minister and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, demonstrated the solid foundation of Malaysia-China ties.
"This time, the prime minister's working visit will not only focus on traditional areas of bilateral relations, but also open avenues for cooperation in new fields of strategic importance to both countries. Malaysia-China relations were previously driven largely by political, trade and investment cooperation.
"However, in recent years, Malaysia under the prime minister's leadership has placed broader emphasis on cooperation in areas such as education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and artificial intelligence (AI)," he told a press conference here today.
Also present was Malaysia's Consul-General in Shanghai, Abdullah Ma'amor Ibrahim. This is Anwar's fourth visit to China since taking office as prime minister in November 2022.
Norman said Anwar is scheduled to attend the opening ceremony of the 46th WorldSkills Competition 2026, deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Opening Plenary Session, and hold a roundtable session with business leaders and captains of industry in Shanghai.
He said Anwar will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Transport Minister Anthony Loke, and senior government officials.
"Anwar is also scheduled to attend the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) in Hangzhou on Thursday, where he will deliver a keynote address and attend the launch of the Mandarin translation of the book 'Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Postnormal Times'," he said.
He said the highlight of the visit will be a bilateral meeting between Anwar and Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the West Lake State Guest House in Hangzhou, followed by a dinner hosted by Li.
"Both leaders are expected to discuss strengthening bilateral ties under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership framework, in line with aspirations to build a High-Level Malaysia-China Strategic Community with a Shared Future, as well as President Xi Jinping's initiatives, including the Global Development Initiative (GDI) and Global Civilisation Initiative (GCI).
"This includes the proposed extension of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project from Kota Baru to Rantau Panjang, which will yield major benefits in connectivity and economic development, alongside upgrading the 'Two Countries, Twin Parks' project following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on April 17, 2025," he said.
Norman said discussions will also cover collaboration in advanced technologies, including AI, green energy, semiconductors and the digital economy, as well as the prime minister's upcoming visit to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Leaders' Summit in November.
He added that on regional and international issues, both leaders are expected to discuss Malaysia's participation as a founding member of the World AI Cooperation Organisation (WAICO) and support for China-led global initiatives, including the Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilisation Initiative and Global Governance Initiative.
"This includes Malaysia's participation as a founding member of the International Alliance Against Telecom and Cyber Fraud to share experiences and best practices in addressing international security issues, particularly cross-border and cybercrime, as well as Malaysia's involvement in BRICS following the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India," he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's participation in WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 forms part of these broader engagement initiatives, alongside sustaining two-way trade momentum, which reached RM456.68 billion (US$113.82 billion) from January to August.
China has remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno seeks release of Najib's frozen assets for RM50m fine [WATCH]
Article:
PARIT: Umno hopes the courts will consider allowing a portion of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's frozen personal assets to be released to pay his RM50 million fine.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said that the party is actively pursuing this effort.
"Yes, we hope the court will take this matter into consideration," he said when asked whether any motion or plan was underway to unfreeze Najib's accounts or assets specifically to settle the fine.
Asyraf, who is also Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) chairman, was speaking to reporters after the closing ceremony of the Deputy Prime Minister's Cup MRSM Debate Competition at Maktab Rendah Sains MARA (MRSM) Parit.
Last week, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia,
granted Najib a conditional pardon
to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
This was subject to Najib meeting certain conditions, including paying a RM50 million fine.
Najib's lawyers, Messrs Shafee & Co, said a significant part of his assets, bank accounts and properties remained
subject to freezing orders
and government enforcement proceedings, with their disposal not presently within his sole control.
Umno has since launched a donation drive to lighten Najib's financial burden in settling the fine.
On the donation drive, Asyraf said that collections were expected to reach RM2 million as of today (Mon).
"We expect the collection to hit RM2 million today. On average, we are seeing additions of RM40,000 to RM50,000 every hour.
"This comes entirely from voluntary contributions. We did not make it mandatory for members. It is open to anyone wishing to help," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian glove makers eye up to US$2.50 price hike in October
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian glove makers plan to raise selling prices by US$2 to US$2.50 per carton in October to offset higher production costs, with another increase possible as early as November, according to RHB Research.
The firm said its channel checks showed producers were preparing to raise prices after generic nitrile glove average selling prices (ASPs) fell to between US$19 and US$20 per 1,000 pieces in September, from a peak of US$27 to US$28 in May.
"The next move is up, and China is leading it," RHB Research analyst Eddy Do said in a note.
He said China's Intco Medical had raised prices by 15 yuan (US$2.24) to 40 yuan (US$5.97) per carton from Sept 9, giving Malaysian manufacturers room to follow with their own increases in October.
Malaysian producers could raise prices again in November if nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) latex costs continue to climb.
However, Do said much of the October increase would merely compensate manufacturers for higher natural gas costs rather than significantly improve their margins.
During the latest results briefings, he said Malaysian producers indicated that generic glove ASPs would need to increase by US$1.50 to US$2 per carton just to cover an expected 40 per cent to 50 per cent rise in gas tariffs in October.
That would leave between zero and US$1 per carton to absorb any further increase in NBR latex prices, the analyst said.
"With second-quarter operating profit of just US$2.43 to US$4.08 per carton for the generic producers, there is little room for error."
Malaysian producers' ability to raise prices is heavily influenced by their Chinese competitors.
Chinese generic nitrile gloves are currently priced at about US$18.50 per carton, only US$0.50 below Malaysia's US$19 for non-US markets.
The gap was US$1.50 to US$2 in early August.
"In other words, China prices have moved up, and this is what gives Malaysian producers room to follow," RHB Research said.
"This is the core of our concern: Malaysian producers do not control their own pricing," it added.
The industry also remains burdened by excess capacity despite the prospect of higher prices.
RHB Research expects global glove supply to remain at 451 billion pieces through 2028, while demand is projected to increase from 344 billion pieces this year to 387 billion in 2028.
This would leave an estimated surplus of 107 billion pieces in 2026, narrowing to 64 billion pieces by 2028.
Malaysia is also losing ground in the United States, where glove makers typically command better prices.
The country's share of US glove imports fell to 50 per cent in July from 62 per cent in December 2025, with Vietnam and Indonesia accounting for almost all of the lost market share.
RHB Research estimated that the decline represented about 14 billion pieces annually that would have to be redirected to non-US markets, where competition with Chinese producers is more direct.
Despite the potential near-term earnings boost from higher prices, the research firm maintained its "Underweight" stance on the glove sector.
"If October's increase is realised in full, fourth-quarter net profit should improve," it said, adding that a few quarters of higher profit per carton would do little to address the industry's longer-term oversupply, which could persist through 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ten ex-Bar presidents urge federal intervention in Negri Sembilan dispute [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ten former presidents of the Malaysian Bar have called on the federal government to step in and resolve the constitutional issues surrounding the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
In a joint statement today, they described the recent developments involving Tuanku Muhriz as raising serious concerns over the constitutional monarchy and rule of law.
"We call on the federal government to step in and finally resolve these troubling issues. This state of affairs sets a dangerous precedent for the constitutional monarchy and the future of this country - a country that must, at all times, chart its course strictly in accordance with the law.
"Such unbecoming and undignified conduct, as well as such utter disrespect for the law, must stop," they said.
The 10 lawyers are Datuk Mah Weng Kwai, Datuk Kuthubul Zaman Bukhari, Datuk Yeo Yang Poh, Datuk Ambiga Sreenevasan, Ragunath Kesavan, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, Christopher Leong, Datuk George Varughese, Salim Bashir and Karen Cheah Yee Lynn.
They said the Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) had purportedly removed Tuanku Muhriz without the process required under Article 10 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959.
They said Article 10 provides for a "complete enquiry by the Undangs" before a ruler could be removed, and questioned whether such an enquiry had been conducted and whether Tuanku Muhriz had been allowed to be heard.
The lawyers also questioned the validity of a purported proclamation dated April 19, 2026, including the circumstances surrounding its signing by the menteri besar on Aug 3.
They said the exco did not have the constitutional power to unilaterally remove a ruler and urged all parties to uphold the Federal Constitution and UUTKNS 1959.
The group also referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers' position that the purported proclamation was invalid and that the menteri besar and exco did not have unilateral power to terminate or vacate the office of the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
They further said the State Secretary's Office had declined to proceed with gazetting the purported proclamation.
"We, the undersigned, call for an immediate and complete halt to this assault on the constitutional sovereignty of the Negri Sembilan monarchy and the rule of law.
"We strongly urge the state government of Negri Sembilan, all public officials, and all citizens of Malaysia to faithfully uphold the Federal Constitution and the UUTKNS 1959, preserve the rule of law, and fully respect the sovereignty and constitutional standing of His Royal Highness Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as the sole, lawful, and reigning Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan," they said.
The lawyers further said the exco is not above the law, and its unlawful conduct in this matter must be curbed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Najib's home inspected as preparations for house arrest continue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police and Prisons Department officers have assessed Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Jalan Langgak Duta as preparations continue for the former prime minister's conditional house arrest.
Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said officers from both agencies inspected the residence this afternoon, including necessary security arrangements should the house-arrest order be implemented.
However, he stressed that the relevant order had yet to be received and arrangements were not finalised.
"It has not been finalised because we have not received the order yet. It will be finalised once the order is completed, as there are conditions involved," he told reporters outside Najib's residence today.
Anuar said the visit involved an assessment of the residence, with police focusing on security aspects while the Prisons Department assessed matters concerning the detention arrangements.
He said police were prepared to provide security at any time, covering both the area surrounding the residence and the necessary security arrangements at the premises.
Under the proposed division of responsibilities, Anuar said the Prisons Department would be responsible for security inside the residence, while police would handle security outside.
He said there were no plans for unusually stringent physical security measures, such as installing barriers or fencing around the house.
"The Prisons Department will be responsible for the inside, while police will be responsible for the outside," he said.
Asked when the arrangements would become official, Anuar reiterated that this would depend on the authorities receiving and completing the relevant order.
His remarks came after police said earlier today that they had yet to receive
official confirmation
concerning Najib's placement under house arrest.
Security preparations have nevertheless been underway around the Langgak Duta residence, with police previously saying a mobile police station would be deployed in the area to facilitate security arrangements.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the stipulated conditions.
Earlier, it was reported that the
RM50 million fine
imposed on Najib, which must be settled before he can serve the remainder of his prison sentence under conditional house arrest, had yet to be paid.
Najib's lawyers, Shafee & Co, said most of his assets, bank accounts and properties remained subject to freezing orders and government enforcement action.
The firm said the disposal of those assets was not entirely within Najib's control, and his ability to pay the RM50 million fine therefore depended partly on matters beyond his control.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amanah wants Negri MB to seek state assembly dissolution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) wants Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to seek the dissolution of the state legislative assembly amid the latest dispute between the state executive and the palace.
Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil said the party took note of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir's decision to withdraw his consent and revoke the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors.
"The party takes note that the political turmoil in Negri Sembilan has reached a very critical stage when the Yang di-Pertuan Besar has withdrawn his consent and revoked the appointments of all members of the Negri Sembilan state executive council who were appointed following the 16th Negri Sembilan state election for breaching their oath," he said in a statement today.
Faiz said Amanah would not interfere in matters concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, which he said should be resolved according to the law, the state Constitution and Negri Sembilan customs.
However, he claimed the 16th state election was triggered by pressure from certain quarters seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz from the throne.
"This is reinforced by the proclamation signed by the menteri besar immediately after the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, on Aug 3," he said.
Faiz said the situation was further aggravated when the menteri besar openly rejected the royal decree.
He also accused Umno of failing to respect the Malay royal institution.
"Umno has failed to respect the position of the Malay royal institution by taking steps to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar from the throne, as though it were an act of coup d'état," he said.
He said such actions were contrary to the wishes of the people of Negri Sembilan, adding that the state election had not been intended to interfere with the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
"Therefore, we urge the menteri besar to seek the dissolution of the Negri Sembilan state legislative assembly, as the confrontation between the executive and the palace is contrary to the spirit and principles of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959.
"We believe that the turmoil, which has not been properly managed by Umno, could also threaten the stability of the state government," he said.
The development followed Tuanku Muhriz's decision to withdraw his consent and revoke the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors with immediate effect.
The palace said the decision was made after the exco members were found to have breached their oath of office. It said the members had taken and signed their oath and pledge of allegiance before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar on Aug 7, before their appointment to the State Executive Council.
Ismail was
subsequently directed
to submit a new list of candidates for the state executive council for the Yang di-Pertuan Besar's consideration and consent.
However, Ismail said any action to dismiss or terminate the membership of a state executive councillor without the advice or request of the menteri besar was a legal error, unconstitutional and had no legal effect.
He said
he had never been consulted
or advised on the termination of any Negri Sembilan exco member under Article 38(5) of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959 (UUTKNS).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court rules developer cannot turn common property into private assets
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has ruled that a property developer cannot turn areas meant for residents' common use into private property before selling them or using them as security for bank loans.
A three-member bench led by Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi unanimously dismissed three appeals involving the PJ Centrestage development in Section 13, Petaling Jaya.
The court upheld a High Court decision that 342 car park bays, seven basement areas, landscaped areas, rooftops, a reception area and external façade spaces were common property belonging to the development and should be managed by the PJ Centrestage Joint Management Body (JMB).
The other members of the bench were Federal Court judge Datuk Azimah Omar and appellate court judge Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril.
Leadmont Properties Sdn Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) filed the appeals against the High Court's June 1, 2022 ruling in favour of the JMB.
The dispute began after PJ Centrestage JMB discovered that several areas it regarded as common property had been registered as strata or accessory parcels.
The JMB alleged that some of these areas were later sold by developer Cherish Springs Sdn Bhd to Leadmont Properties Sdn Bhd.
Leadmont later obtained financing from Hong Leong Bank and Maybank using interests in the properties as security, prompting the banks to become involved in the dispute.
Azizah, who wrote the grounds of judgment, said the disputed areas were common property under the Building and Common Property (Maintenance and Management) Act 2007 (BCPA).
The court said the BCPA applied because the sale and purchase agreements and disputed transactions took place while the law was still in force.
"We therefore find no error in the High Court's conclusion that the BCPA 2007 applies to the factual matrix of these appeals," she said.
The court found that the approved building plans did not originally show the 342 car park bays and seven basement areas as accessory parcels.
Azizah said the landscaped areas, Level 6 and Level 14 rooftops and the reception area were also shown in the approved plans as common areas rather than private accessory parcels.
"Their subsequent attempt to excise the disputed common property as accessory parcels was only conceived later and constitutes an afterthought aimed at depriving the plaintiff of the property that was always intended to be and/or remain as common property."
The court also affirmed the High Court's finding of fraud and false representation in the registration of strata titles over the disputed areas.
It said the developer had wrongly represented to the Selangor Land Office that the disputed areas were not common property.
The court also agreed with the High Court that Cherish Springs and Leadmont were guilty of "fraud and/or false misrepresentation."
The court said the registration of the disputed strata titles had deprived buyers of their contractual and legal rights to use the common areas.
The court noted that the two companies were closely linked, shared the same registered and office addresses and company secretary, and were effectively controlled by the same family.
Azizah also criticised the banks for failing to carry out sufficient checks before granting the loans and rejected their claims to security interests over the disputed property.
"They failed to carry out proper due diligence to verify whether the Cherish Springs and Leadmont had any valid registered or equitable interest in the disputed common property before granting the loans to the latter," she added.
The court held that the banks' security interests over the property were invalid even though they had granted the loans without knowing that the disputed property had been unlawfully acquired.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korean soldiers among three injured in DMZ mine blast
Article:
SEOUL: Three people, including South Korean soldiers, were injured in a suspected mine blast inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), South Korea's Yonhap TV reported on Monday.
The DMZ, which has divided the peninsula since the 1950-53 Korean war ended with an armistice, is among the most heavily mined places in the world.
"A soldier was seriously injured during an operation in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) involving the 25th Infantry Division," a military official said, referring to the buffer zone separating the two Koreas.
Yonhap TV reported that three soldiers were injured in the incident, and were taken to the Armed Forces Capital Hospital.
It was not yet clear whether the mine was planted by North Korean forces or belonged to the South Korean military, Yonhap TV said.
Around 800,000 mines are estimated to be buried around the area, according to military data cited by the Yonhap news agency, many dating to the Korean War although mine-laying has continued in recent years.
In 2024, after North Korean leader Kim Jong Un designated South Korea as his country's "principal enemy", Pyongyang's military spent months laying mines and building anti-tank barriers along the border as part of efforts to permanently seal off the frontier.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran warns US of new weapons, targets if attacks resume
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Monday warned they would attack new targets and deploy new weapons if the US launches further attacks on the country.
Almost seven months into their war, Teheran and Washington remain locked in a stalemate, though neither side appears willing to return to full-scale war.
In a statement, a spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said "there will certainly be significant changes in our defence and our counteroffensive" in the event of a new US attack.
"We will introduce new weapons with new capabilities into the battlefield, and the world will be surprised," he said.
"Our targets will not necessarily be the same as before either. We have new targets that have not yet been attacked."
The Guards also said they were prepared for a "prolonged war."
On Saturday, the central command of Iran's military said the US was planning new action against Teheran, according to state television, but it did not elaborate.
Fighting between the US and Iran has eased in recent days after a flare-up at the end of last month, though Teheran continues sporadic attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Both sides are maintaining rival blockades in the waterway in an effort to exert pressure.
The war has spread to Yemen, with the country's Iran-backed Houthis taking more territory from the Saudi-backed government and the group launching attacks on Saudi targets, including the capital Riyadh.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sentul police chief, prisons officers at Najib's residence for house arrest preparations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam and Prisons Department officers arrived at Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Jalan Langgak Duta today amid preparations for the former prime minister's conditional house arrest.
It is understood that a meeting involving police and Prisons Department officers was held this afternoon to discuss procedures and security arrangements for the house arrest.
Several official government vehicles were seen entering the compound of Najib's residence from 2pm.
Anuar Bakri arrived at 2.20pm, followed by Prisons Department officers at 3.15pm.
The meeting includes discussions on procedures and security measures for guarding a person serving a sentence under house arrest.
As of 3.30pm, the meeting was ongoing.
When contacted, Anuar Bakri confirmed he was at the residence.
Earlier, it was reported that the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib, which must be settled before he can serve the remainder of his prison sentence under conditional house arrest,
had yet to be paid
.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the payment must be made at the Kuala Lumpur High Court registry as the case originated and was heard there.
"So far, Datuk Seri Najib's family has not paid the fine. Once payment is made, I cannot say exactly when Datuk Seri Najib will be brought home. It may take some time," he said.
He added that procedures governing Najib's house arrest would be handled by the Prisons Department.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Imran Khan's three sisters arrested as Pakistan opposition plans protest
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan's party said on Monday that his three sisters had been arrested.
"Punjab police have raided Aleem Khan's home and have abducted Imran Khan's other two sisters, his nephews and their children," Zulfi Bukhari, a spokesman for Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, said on his social media platform X.
"Khan's sisters and their children were taken into custody, but the children were released," PTI's information secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told AFP.
"All three sisters have been sent to Kot Lakhpat Jail, Lahore," he added.
The law enforcement agencies arrested Khan's sisters Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Khan from Lahore, the capital city of Punjab province.
The deputy commissioner of Lahore on Sunday passed two separate orders, the copies of which were seen by AFP, for the three sisters' 30-day detention under the Maintenance of Public Order law of Punjab province.
Punjab police did not respond to AFP's request for comment.
Khan's party has announced a protest call for Sept 27.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Sunday the protest call was illegal.
"We will not allow them to block roads and disrupt people's lives," Tarar said.
Khan has been in jail since 2023 and was sentenced late last year, along with his wife, to 17 years in jail on corruption charges they both deny.
The 73-year-old Khan, who was also a former Pakistan cricket captain, was prime minister from 2018 to 2022 before being removed in a no-confidence vote during a political crisis over tensions between his government and Pakistan's powerful military establishment.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men from China fined RM4,700 each over crypto investment scam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Two men from China were fined RM4,700 each by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to conspiring to carry out a bogus online cryptocurrency investment scam earlier this month.
Chen Le, 36, and Zhong Guoxuan, 31, pleaded guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab.
The court then imposed a RM4,700 fine on each accused.
They were charged with being party to a criminal conspiracy under Section 120B(2) of the Penal Code by agreeing to commit an unlawful act involving a non-existent online cryptocurrency investment scheme.
The offence was allegedly committed at Marina View Resort, Bandar Baru Permas Jaya, at 1.09pm on Sept 11.
The charge was read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code for common intention.
Section 120B(2) provides for up to six months' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Sarah Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal appeared for the prosecution.
Both accused were unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China confirms Xi to visit US this week for Trump talks
Article:
BEIJING: China's leader Xi Jinping will visit the United States this week for talks with President Donald Trump, Beijing confirmed on Monday.
Xi will be there from Wednesday to Friday, a government statement said.
Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said the two leaders would "have an in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-US relations and world peace and development."
Beijing would "work with the US to enrich the substance of the relationship of constructive strategic stability between China and the US, strengthen dialogue and cooperation, (and) properly manage differences", he added.
Washington had already made clear that the leaders of the world's two biggest economies were due to meet this week, in what is expected to be a bid to ease tensions over trade, technology and broader strategic issues.
Trump will personally welcome Xi at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday before their meetings the following day, a US official confirmed. The US leader was welcomed by China's vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.
"I'll be discussing almost everything with him," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday.
The simmering trade war between the two countries is a key concern, and the threat of military confrontation over Taiwan looms large as well.
While both sides have maintained a tariff truce for nearly a year, they have yet to secure a lasting agreement.
Vice Premier He Lifeng, China's top negotiator for trade, is in the United States for meetings with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
The two discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, as they met on Sunday.
Trump's Iran war casts a long shadow too, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran, despite reports that Beijing supplied Iran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Riverbank protection project brings relief to Kampung Pulau Pisang residents
Article:
KOTA BARU: Residents of Kampung Pulau Pisang, who have endured severe riverbank erosion for years are breathing a sigh of relief following the implementation of a federal riverbank protection project.
Kampung Pulau Pisang village head Zainab Deraman said the erosion worsened last December, with several stretches along the Kelantan River badly affected.
"Almost all areas along the Kelantan River are at risk of erosion, with some sections suffering severe bank collapses.
"The situation has also affected fishermen, who sometimes have to stop going to sea due to unsafe conditions," she said when met at the site.
Zainab said several houses had also been affected by the erosion, but residents received immediate assistance when necessary.
She said the riverbank protection project, which began in Kampung Pulau Pisang about two months ago, had brought relief to residents who had long been worried about the safety of their homes and livelihoods.
Self-employed Mohd Azmi Mohamed Abdul Ghani said the project had given residents greater peace of mind, particularly with the monsoon season approaching.
"Before this, many of us could not sleep, fearing the erosion would worsen and the riverbank would collapse again.
"But after seeing the progress of the project, we are grateful," said the 48-year-old.
"But after seeing the progress of the project, we are grateful," said the 48-year-old.
Meanwhile, Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department director Farhan Sufyan Borhan said several areas along the Kelantan and Golok rivers remained at risk of recurring riverbank erosion and landslides, particularly settlements located close to riverbanks.
He said the risks had been identified based on previous incidents, including areas around Kampung Gaung Pendek and Kampung Jalan Pohon Celagi in Pasir Mas, as well as Kampung Pulau Pisang.
He said the risk along the Golok River involved settlements stretching from Rantau Panjang to Pasir Mas, where erosion could cause sections of the riverbank to collapse.
"Other areas of concern include Kuala Krai, particularly around Lata Rek and Kampung Cucur Puteri.
"However, the situation in Lojing and Jeli is different as the landslide risk there is mainly associated with roads and access routes used for transportation, as well as plantation areas, rather than densely populated settlements," he said.
Farhan said that in areas along rivers, the risk centred on the riverbanks, adding that previous incidents showed the locations remained vulnerable.
"Based on previous incidents, these locations remain vulnerable and the possibility of similar incidents occurring again cannot be ruled out," he said.
Farhan said the department was also focusing on raising public awareness so residents living near vulnerable areas would know the necessary safety measures to take in the event of erosion, landslides or other emergencies.
He said the department had a Special Tactical Operation Malaysia (STORM) team in Kelantan, comprising personnel trained and equipped to conduct search-and-rescue operations involving collapsed buildings, roads and other structures.
"We cannot prevent every incident from happening, but awareness campaigns are important to ensure residents know what steps to take when such incidents occur," he said.
