Title: Cops confirm arson at two 24-hour convenience stores in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 21 — Two 24-hour convenience stores here were targeted by unknown persons in separate arson attacks on Sunday night.
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the incidents occurred between 7.05pm and 8.30pm.
“The first incident, which occurred in the King Centre area, involved the use of firecrackers and did not result in any losses.
“In the second incident along Jalan Green, two male suspects came to the premises and threw an object inside, causing two explosions and a fire,” he said in a statement on Monday.
The fire was extinguished by Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) personnel.
Alexson said police are investigating both incidents under Section 436 of the Penal Code, for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy.
Conviction carries up to 20 years’ imprisonment and possible fine.
“PDRM Sarawak is actively conducting investigations to track down and arrest the suspects, analyse the materials used, examine closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and determine whether there is any link between the two incidents.
“The motive is still under investigation, and the cases are being investigated under Section 436 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy a house or building,” he said in a statement on Monday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the two suspects had a similar modus operandi, with both masked and dressed in dark clothing before entering the premises and throwing objects believed to contain explosive or flammable materials into the stores.
Mohamad Zainal said police would also investigate claims circulating that the convenience stores were selling online gambling ‘top-ups’ and take appropriate action, including applying to the local authorities to revoke their business licences.
“The public is advised against making speculation that could jeopardise the investigation.
“Owners of business premises are advised to enhance security measures and immediately report to the police if they detect any suspicious individuals or vehicles,” he stressed.
He said efforts are ongoing to trace and identify those behind the attacks.
“Members of the public with information on the incidents are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Tan Chiang Fook on 018-2628805 or the Kuching district police headquarters operations room on 082-244444,” he said.
Meanwhile, Bomba in a separate statement said a call on the fire at the Jalan Green convenience store was received at 8.19pm.
It said the fire damaged 35 per cent of the store, starting at the front and spreading towards the centre of the shop.
“No injuries were reported in the incident. Personnel from the Batu Lintang and Padungan fire stations wrapped up the operation at 9.03pm after ensuring there was no risk of the fire reigniting,” the department said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Man found dead in petrol station toilet near Tronoh
Article:
IPOH, Sept 21 — A 39-year-old local man was found dead inside the toilet of a petrol station in Taman Tronoh Baru, near Tronoh, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they received an emergency call at 2:20pm before a team of personnel from the Batu Gajah Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene at 2:34pm.
“Upon arrival, the police and the Ministry of Health (MOH) were already at the scene and found a man lying unconscious, as well as stuck in the toilet door frame.
“The victim was later confirmed dead by the MOH, and it was informed that the victim was a member of the public who had stopped by to use the toilet at the petrol station,” he said in a statement today.
He said firemen then carried out operations to extricate the victim, who was stuck in the door frame, by adjusting the victim’s position until he was successfully removed from the toilet.
He added that the victim’s body was brought out and handed over to the police for further action before the operation fully concluded at 3pm. — Bernama

Title: ‘Urgent and important’: Serikin border complex fast-tracked for 2027 completion, says minister
Article:
BAU, Sept 21 — Construction of the RM43.66 million Serikin Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex has recorded 11.23 per cent physical progress as of yesterday and is expected to be completed by the end of next year.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the border security project under the National Security Council (MKN) was placed in the ‘urgent and important’ category for fast-track implementation.
“This project is also among the matters discussed in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Meeting as well as the MA63 Technical Committee Council.
“This is important. It is among the government’s efforts to ensure border projects can be upgraded so that we can safeguard the country’s sovereignty, especially in Sabah and Sarawak,” he told reporters after conducting a working visit to the project site here today.
The construction project includes the main building and inspection counters, four units of quarters, a surau, a canteen, a guardhouse, as well as mechanical and electrical services.
Commenting on the challenges of the project, Mustapha said logistics, road construction and the provision of electricity, water and telecommunications services needed to be given special attention to avoid operational delays once the building was completed.
Meanwhile, Mustapha, who also visited the border control post (PKS) project site in Telok Melano-Temajuk, said the project was in the final phase of the tender process for the appointment of a contractor before the issuance of the Letter of Acceptance (SST).
He said the PKS was expected to be completed in another two years.
“Do not consider projects involving national security as ordinary projects. This is actually what needs to be understood by all agencies, departments, ministries, contractors and other parties involved in this project,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh: Loke’s resignation offer was DAP CEC’s final decision, must be respected
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister was the final decision of the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and must be respected.
DAP CEC deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh said the CEC meeting last Saturday also heard various proposals and views before the decision was made.
“The CEC held a lengthy meeting, and various proposals and views were put forward. The final decision, the CEC’s decision; this is the highest decision-making body, was that YB Anthony Loke offered to resign.
“That was the CEC’s decision. I do not want to disclose the other discussions as they were part of the CEC deliberations, but we have to respect the decision made by the CEC,” she said at a press conference on the 2026 Deepavali Bazaar here today.
Hannah said this in response to the DAP CEC’s decision following its meeting on the party’s stance on the issue of a conditional pardon for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Last Saturday, Loke offered to resign as Transport Minister following DAP’s stance on the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
Loke said the resignation would only involve him as a member of the Cabinet, while the other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the government to ensure continued political stability in the country. — Bernama

Title: Beyond trade: Anwar’s fourth China visit targets AI, digital economy and skills
Article:
SHANGHAI, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou beginning Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development.
In his three-day working visit on the invitation of the Chinese government, Anwar’s robust itinerary centres on a high-level bilateral meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, alongside engagements at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 and the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou.
“This is the prime minister’s fourth visit to China (since becoming prime minister in 2022). This shows how familiar and close the relationship between Malaysia and China is.”
“Although this is a working visit, the prime minister has been honoured by Premier Li Qiang with a bilateral meeting between Malaysia and China, and also a dinner to be held in Hangzhou,” Malaysia’s Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad told the Malaysian media ahead of the prime minister’s arrival here on Tuesday.
He said Anwar’s visit also aimed at initiating cooperation in new fields outside of traditional fields, such as education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), digital economy and AI.
The prime minister will also deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 and at the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The prime minister is scheduled to hold talks with Li in Hangzhou, providing both leaders with another opportunity to review bilateral projects and explore strategic cooperation of the countries.
Norman said that during the meeting, the two leaders are expected to discuss several matters to strengthen bilateral relations under the framework of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, in line with the aspiration of building a High-Level Strategic Malaysia–China Community with a Shared Future and President Xi Jinping’s initiatives including the Global Development Initiative (GDI) and the Global Civilisation Initiative (GCI).
Norman said the bilateral meeting was also expected to discuss the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) extension project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang which will benefit connectivity and economic development.
Also discussed was the implementation of the upgrading of the Two Countries, Twin Parks project following the signing of a memorandum of understanding on April 17, 2025.
Apart from that, it also touched on the prime minister’s visit to Shenzhen in conjunction with the Apec Leaders’ Summit to be held in November this year as well as Malaysia’s participation as a founding member country of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO).
While in Hangzhou, Anwar is also scheduled to launch a book titled
Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform and Ignorance in Postnormal Times
which has been translated into Chinese.
Norman said China had remained Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) for the period of January to August.
Anwar is also slated to meet Chinese captains of industry as part of efforts to attract quality investments into Malaysia.
The session is expected to showcase investment opportunities in data centres, AI, semiconductors, electric vehicles, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, logistics and the digital economy. — Bernama

Title: KL mayor: Sunday flash floods hit city after Ampang, Lembah Keramat record 155mm rainfall
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas.
Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital.
“Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.
“As of 5.30pm, Lembah Keramat recorded the highest accumulated rainfall at 155.5 mm, compared with the usual 30 mm,” he said during a press conference here today.
According to media reports, heavy rain that swept across the federal capital on Sunday afternoon resulted in flooding in several areas, including Ampang, Taman U-Thant and Jalan Ampang, disrupting traffic.
On the issue of foreign worker accommodation at the Federal Territory Affordable Housing Project (Residensi Max) on Jalan Kolam Air, Fadlun said the Commissioner of Buildings (COB) had warned the project developer against converting utility rooms into accommodation for foreign workers.
“Residensi Max remains under the developer’s supervision. Therefore, the COB has issued a warning letter to the developer, reminding the developer not to house workers in areas or rooms designated for other purposes, and we will continue to monitor the situation,” he said.
The media had previously reported concerns among Residensi Max residents over the presence of foreign nationals at the residence, with the situation allegedly having persisted for nearly a year.
Residensi Max Residents’ Association chairman Muhammed Assyafiq Ahmad Kamal reportedly expressed frustration with the management, alleging that it had refused to cooperate with residents to resolve the issue. — Bernama

Title: Selangor expands Kita Selangor Voucher eligibility, households earning RM8,000 or below now qualify
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — The Selangor government has expanded the eligibility threshold for the Kita Selangor Voucher (BKS) to include households with a monthly income of RM8,000 or below.
State Women’s Development and Social Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said the phased rollout of the programme was introduced under the Selangor Resilience Strengthening Package to assist citizens affected by the rising cost of living and economic uncertainty resulting from global supply crises.
It initially prioritised vulnerable groups such as single mothers and heads of hardcore-poor households before extending eligibility to households earning RM5,000 or less.
“The state government has further expanded the eligibility threshold to include households earning RM8,000 or less. Applications must be submitted via the SELangkah app,” she said in a statement today.
She said applicants who are currently under review, were previously rejected, or are appealing will have their cases reassessed under the revised criteria,” she said.
The key requirements include Malaysian citizen and a registered voter residing in Selangor.
“Married couples or single parents must have at least one child aged 18 or younger and a household income of RM8,000 or less.
“Only one recipient is allowed per household, and the applicant must not be an active recipient of the Selangor Prosperous Living Aid (BINGKAS) programme,” she said.
For further information regarding eligibility criteria, the application process, and implementation, please visit the official BKS portal at https://baucarkitaselangor.com/. — Bernama

Title: JPJ nets RM91.2m from ‘H’ series plates, confirms RM10.7m winning bid for ‘H 1’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — The Road Transport Department, better known by its Malay initials JPJ, collected RM91.2 million from bidding for the new “H” series special registration numbers (NPI), with a single plate, H 1, fetching RM10,777,777, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) said today.
In a media statement, the ministry said the total of RM91,206,642 came from bidding held entirely on the JPJeBid system from Sept 16 to 20.
Of that, RM89,266,542 was bid revenue and RM1,940,100 was service fees. The series was introduced to mark Malaysia Day 2026.
A total of 34,664 bidders took part, and 8,223 registration numbers were successfully bid on. That works out to an average of roughly RM10,860 per number sold, based on the bid revenue.
H 1 was the highest bid by a wide margin. The next highest was H 9 at RM4,969,999, followed by H 3 at RM4,209,777, H 5 at RM4,007,777 and H 8 at RM4 million. H 6 went for RM3.38 million, H 2 for RM3.18 million and H 7 for RM3.1 million. H 4 fetched RM2,437,777 and H 11 RM1,557,777.
The numbers that drew the most bidders were H 1001 and H 100, with 37 each. They were followed by H 1805 with 36 bidders, and H 1777 and H 4818 with 32 each.
The ministry called the result proof of the success of the government’s digital transformation through JPJeBid, which it said makes bidding easier, faster, more efficient and more transparent.
It said all proceeds will go back to the public through MOT and JPJ programmes, including road safety and initiatives that benefit the community directly.

Title: Putrajaya condemns Al-Aqsa storming, warns provocations risk sparking wider global conflict
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first qibla and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended.
“History proves that barbaric incursions into al-Aqsa have always been the catalyst for a wave of awakening among the ummah.
“The Zionist regime cannot be allowed to normalise these extremist actions, which risk pushing the world into a more complex global conflict,” he said in a statement today.
In light of this, Zulkifli urged the international community to take immediate and firm action against the Zionist regime, rather than merely issuing rhetorical condemnations.
He also called on Muslims in the country to continue uniting in solidarity and performing the qunut nazilah prayer so that Allah SWT may preserve the sanctity of the Al-Aqsa Mosque and liberate Palestinian land from the grip of tyranny.
The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB seeks Federal Court ruling, says Malaysia should hear fraud claims against UK law firm
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court’s ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm.
Lawyer Lim Zhi Ying, one of the lawyers representing 1MDB, confirmed the notice of motion was filed on Aug 28, this year.
She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application.
In its application, 1MDB sought leave to appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision, citing that there are important questions of general principles to be decided for the first time by the top court.
1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.
Among the questions include whether in determining the forum conveniens (an appropriate forum) for a claim in conspiracy involving alleged conspirators across multiple jurisdictions, the relevant connecting factors to be assessed by reference to the alleged conspiracy as a whole, including the places where the other alleged conspirators and material witnesses are located, and not by reference to the circumstances and location of the particular foreign defendant challenging jurisdiction.
On Aug 20, this year, a three-member bench comprising Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, allowed White and Case LLB’s appeal, ruling that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm.
Justice Muniandy, who delivered the unanimous decision, held that the requirements under the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 and the Rules of Court 2012 for the service of proceedings outside Malaysia had not been satisfied.
He said 1MDB failed to prove that Malaysia is clearly the forum convenient to hear this suit, adding that Patrick Mahony, a director of PetroSaudi International Ltd, is a foreign national residing outside Malaysia and therefore could not serve as a proper “anchor defendant” to justify the service of proceedings out of jurisdiction.
The panel also set aside the High Court’s decision to consolidate 1MDB’s suit against White & Case with a separate suit filed by the sovereign wealth fund against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
1MDB filed the suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US$1.83 billion and US$33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony. The fund alleged that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
The alleged misconduct relates to two corporate transactions: the 2009 joint venture with PetroSaudi International, known as the Good Star phase, and the 2010 restructuring of 1MDB’s stake in the joint venture, which 1MDB claims resulted in significant financial losses.
The writ of summons was served out of jurisdiction on White & Case at their UK offices, and the firm subsequently applied to set aside the service, seeking a declaration that the Malaysian court had no jurisdiction to hear the suit.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case’s challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: ‘Possibly the most effective transport minister’: Lim Guan Eng praises Loke’s RM21b infrastructure legacy in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 21 — DAP Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng said today that Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s impending departure from the federal Cabinet represents a major loss for Penang, crediting him with securing federal approval for more than RM21 billion in critical transport infrastructure for the state.
In a press statement, the former Penang chief minister detailed the federal investments championed by Loke during his ministerial tenure.
These include the RM16.8 billion Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) project, the RM1.55 billion expansion of the Penang International Airport (PIA), and RM30 million in upgrades for Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTM) stations, alongside RM2.2 billion for Penang Port and RM500 million for the Swettenham Pier Cruise Terminal.
“With RM 21 billion of approved transportation projects in Penang, Loke is possibly the most effective transport minister who has done the most for Penang compared to the series of MCA transport ministers before him,” Lim said.
Lim said that Penang’s 1.8 million residents deeply appreciate Loke’s willingness to sacrifice his executive post on principle and will remain grateful for his transformative contributions to the state’s transport network.
Lim explained that Loke offered his resignation to reaffirm DAP’s stand on the RM52 billion 1MDB scandal, whether serving in government or in opposition.
He said the party remains steadfast in demanding that those responsible for the financial scandal face justice, describing Loke’s move as an expression of DAP’s “polite disagreement” with the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Loke, who serves as DAP secretary-general and Seremban MP, announced on Saturday that he had offered to step down from the transport portfolio.
The decision followed a nearly three-hour emergency DAP central executive committee (CEC) meeting at the party’s national headquarters in Pudu.Loke clarified that he would retain his party leadership and parliamentary seat, and confirmed that all other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s unity administration.
Speaking on Sunday, Anwar said he had not yet received a formal resignation letter and intended to meet with Loke to hear his views before making any final decision.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board announced on Friday that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon. Under the decree,
Najib will serve the remainder of his SRC International custodial sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to settling a RM50 million fine alongside other statutory conditions.

Title: Malaysia’s air quality improves slightly, but Kapit and Serian remain shrouded in haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Air quality in Kapit, Sarawak, deteriorated steadily throughout the day, overtaking other hotspots to become the most polluted location in Malaysia as of 4pm today.
According to Department of Environment (DoE) data, Kapit recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 173, climbing from 166 logged at 8.30am.
Nationwide, a total of 17 monitoring stations remained in the “Unhealthy” bracket (API 101 to 200), down from the 21 affected stations reported earlier in the morning.
IPD Serian in Sarawak, which held the morning’s highest reading at 168, remained unchanged in the afternoon to rank second nationally. Sibu and Sri Aman followed jointly at 163, with Sibu registering a sharp increase from 156 earlier in the day.
Sarawak accounts for majority of affected areas
Sarawak remained by far the hardest-hit state, accounting for 10 of the 17 unhealthy stations nationwide.
Beyond the top four hotspots, elevated pollution levels were recorded in Bintulu (161), Samalaju (158), Kuching (157), Samarahan (155), and Miri (153). Sarikei was the sole station in the state below the 150 mark, registering 106.
In the Klang Valley, Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded 156, the highest reading in Peninsular Malaysia, closely followed by Putrajaya at 155. Both stations showed minimal variation from morning levels.
Negeri Sembilan also remained in the unhealthy range, though readings eased slightly, with Nilai at 155 (down from 158) and Seremban at 152 (down from 155).
In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu registered 151, a slight improvement from 153 in the morning.
Improvements in Selangor
Selangor recorded the most significant improvement of the day. Johan Setia saw its API drop from 153 to 124, while Shah Alam improved from 152 to 120, though both remained within the unhealthy threshold.
Several stations across the country improved sufficiently to exit the unhealthy category entirely by 4pm, including Kota Kinabalu city in Sabah, Bukit Rambai in Melaka, Tangkak in Johor, alongside ILP Miri and Limbang in Sarawak.
The DoE confirmed that round-the-clock air quality surveillance remains active nationwide, advising the public, especially vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and monitor real-time updates as wind and hotspot patterns shift.

Title: Former deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong dies at 86
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 21 — Former deputy rural development minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who also served as the Kota Belud Member of Parliament, died at the age of 86 at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital, Kuala Lumpur, at about 6am today.
The death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post today, although the cause of death has yet to be confirmed.
“May Allah SWT forgive his sins, shower him with His mercy, and grant him Jannatul Firdaus. Aamiin. Please keep Papa in your doa,” Masley wrote in the post.
He said the remains would be taken to Nurul Islam Mosque in Ampang for bathing and funeral prayers before burial after the Zohor prayers.
Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.
He also served as the Tempasuk state assemblyman on the United Sabah National Organisation (USNO) ticket from 1985 to 1986.
Yahya began his political career in 1981 when he contested the Usukan state seat on the Parti Bersatu Rakyat Jelata Sabah (Berjaya) ticket.
He later contested the Papar parliamentary seat as a PKR candidate in the 2013 General Election. —Bernama

Title: Deepavali Bazaar fees slashed 85pc, Hannah Yeoh sets RM400 cap in Brickfields
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Participation fees for Kuala Lumpur’s 2026 Deepavali Bazaar have been cut by 85 per cent to a maximum of RM400, including the deposit, as part of efforts to reduce costs for traders.
This year’s RM400 fee comprises a RM30 licence fee, RM150 service charge, RM150 site rental and RM70 deposit.
In comparison, traders had to pay RM2,626 in 2025, comprising a RM21 licence fee, RM105 service charge, RM500 site rental and RM2,000 deposit.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the new rate was in line with that charged for Ramadan bazaars, while the trading period would be extended to 30 days from 21 previously.
“Our focus is simple – we want to reduce costs for traders and give them a longer period to do business. The number of lots has also increased this year, consistent with our approach of reducing the cost of doing business for traders in Kuala Lumpur.
“The benefits will reach both traders and city residents. Anyone interested should apply directly to Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL). I do not want middlemen charging thousands of ringgit when we have set the fee at only RM400,” she told a press conference on the bazaar today.
Also present was Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud.
The 2026 Deepavali Bazaar will run from Oct 9 to Nov 7 at two locations, namely at the Tun Sambanthan Complex car park and at Jalan Bunus 6 off Jalan Masjid India.
Under the Mega Deepavali concept, a total of 172 trading lots will be available across the two locations, along with bazaar trader licences and temporary entertainment and promotional licences.
Another 30 temporary entertainment and promotional licences will be available to premises along Jalan Tun Sambanthan, subject to applications from their owners.
According to Fadlun, this year’s bazaar would adopt a hybrid management model, with DBKL retaining responsibility for licensing, regulation and enforcement while associations assist with operations.
The four participating associations are Pertubuhan Kebajikan Peniaga dan Penjaja Kecil Interaksi Kuala Lumpur & Selangor (PKPPKI), Persatuan Prihatin Peniaga Little India Brickfields, Persatuan Penjaja Medan Selera Pines Bazaar Brickfields and Malaysia Hindu Sangam Wilayah Persekutuan.
“We have advertised the bazaar and expect strong interest from the associations. The balloting process will take place on Sept 22 and 23,” Fadlun said.
Addressing concerns over possible traffic congestion around Jalan Tun Sambanthan during the bazaar, he said DBKL had considered the issue before selecting the location.
“We looked at this from the outset before identifying the bazaar site. We have considered alternative routes and will ensure strict traffic control throughout the bazaar period,” he said. — Bernama

Title: AG: Najib’s family hasn’t paid RM50m fine, house arrest still on hold
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 21 — Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak has yet to pay the RM50 million fine stipulated as a condition for serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the fine must be paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office, as the case was filed and heard there.
“As of now, Datuk Seri Najib’s family has not paid the fine. Once payment is made, I cannot say exactly when Datuk Seri Najib will be brought home, as the process may take some time,” he said when contacted by the media today.
He added that the standard operating procedures for the implementation of the house-arrest arrangement would be issued by the Malaysian Prison Department.
A Bernama check at the Kajang Prison today found no activity involving the former Pekan Member of Parliament.
Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence at the Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.
On Sept 18, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence for the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The arrangement is subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with the stipulated conditions. — Bernama

Title: Sabah electricity reserve margin rises to 19pc, expected 26pc by year‑end, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 21 — Sabah’s electricity generation reserve margin has risen from a low of eight per cent in 2024 to 19 per cent as of August this year and is expected to reach 26 per cent by year-end, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said.
He said the System Average Interruption Duration Index (Saidi) had also improved significantly, from 598 minutes in 2023 to 226 minutes as of July this year.
“This is in line with the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan (SE-Ramp 2040) and the target of achieving a 50 per cent renewable energy capacity mix by 2035,” he said in a statement after chairing the Sabah Energy Council meeting at Menara Kinabalu here today.
Hajiji said the improvements were the result of various initiatives to continuously strengthen the state’s electricity grid.
He said Sabah’s energy sector needed to be strengthened comprehensively, including ensuring the readiness of transmission and distribution infrastructure to improve the system’s reliability and resilience.
The meeting also discussed the review of the Long-Term Demand Forecast Study (LTDF2026) and Electricity Generation Development Plan (PDP2026) for the next 10 years to ensure generation capacity planning keeps pace with electricity demand.
Hajiji said plans were also underway to develop gas-fired power plants in Sandakan and Tawau to replace higher-cost diesel and Medium Fuel Oil (MFO) plants.
“Additional Large Scale Solar (LSS) capacity and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), implemented through a competitive bidding process, will also support the strengthening of the generation system,” he said.
He said LSS and BESS projects were also being implemented specifically to improve the reliability of electricity generation on the east coast.
The Chief Minister said Sabah’s electricity supply system had shown significant improvement since the state took over regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy.
“Previously, we had to wait four to five years to obtain approval for applications from the Federal Energy Commission, but since taking over, we can implement them ourselves and improve our electricity supply system more quickly,” he said.
Sabah assumed regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy following the approval of the Electricity Supply Enactment 2024, Sabah Renewable Energy Enactment 2024 and amendments to the Sabah Energy Commission Enactment 2023 by the State Legislative Assembly on Jan 3, 2024. — Bernama

Title: ‘Not true’, says Prisons Department as singer Yasin alleges ‘taiko’ bosses rule jail life
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 21 — The Malaysian Prisons Department has denied claims by singer-composer Yasin Sulaiman that life in prison depends on money and influence.
Prisons Department senior director of prison policy Mohamad Rosidek Musa said the claim was untrue, as it has standard operating procedures (SOP) to handle misconduct or negative incidents among inmates.
“The claim is untrue. In the prison system, we focus on rehabilitation programmes and address negative occurrences.
“We admit certain incidents may happen, but not to the extent alleged. Many released from prison succeed in building new lives, so why focus on the negative aspects?” he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the Malaysian Prisons Department Bookathon Programme 2026 at Pengkalan Chepa Prison here today.
Earlier, Yasin claimed during an episode of the AididitMyWay podcast that a hierarchy existed among inmates, including groups referred to as “bos” and “taiko”, while also alleging that drugs could be smuggled into prison if an individual possessed money and influence.
Mohamad Rosidek said any misconduct is dealt with according to established rules and procedures and that SOPs are continually improved.
“We will address every infraction and take action according to set rules and procedures. Each year, we tighten our SOPs and review them step by step,” he said.
He said conditions at Pengkalan Chepa Prison remain under control, although overcrowding is still an issue the department is addressing.
“Conditions at Pengkalan Chepa Prison are under control because we have satellite prisons and inmate reintegration programmes allowing prisoners to work outside. We are working to overcome overcrowding to ensure proper inmate management, he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Rosidek said the Malaysian Prisons Department Bookathon Programme 2026 received a donation of 10,000 books for inmates nationwide, excluding Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the programme, launched in February, was organised in collaboration with Boustead Holdings Berhad, Royale Chulan, and Syarikat Muda Osman Sdn Bhd (SMO) to encourage the public to donate new or used books for inmates.
“The donations comprise various reading materials, including motivational, fiction, and religious books, while SMO also offered a 20 per cent discount on books purchased and donated through campaigns across its 31 outlets,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Ex‑farmers’ group manager faces 27 forged document charges in RM540,000 oil palm deals
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — A former Area Farmers Organisation (PPK) marketing manager today claimed trial in the Sessions Court here to 27 charges of using forged documents involving oil palm purchases worth more than RM500,000.
Airulnizam Island, 44, who held the position at Bernam Jaya PPK in Sabak Bernam made the plea after all 27 charges were read out before Sessions Court Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.
According to the charges, he had dishonestly used documents as genuine, namely purchase invoices issued by TRC Sawit Sdn Bhd to Bernam Jaya PPK, involving transactions totalling RM540,238.38 between January 2020 and December 2022.
The offences were allegedly committed at Bernam Jaya, Lot PT 608, Simpang 4, Bagan Nakhoda Omar, Sabak Bernam.
The accused, who is also a civil servant with a government agency in Penang, was charged under Section 471 of the Penal Code, punishable under Section 465 of the same law by up to two years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) prosecuting officer Mohd Alimi Mustapha proposed bail of RM50,000, with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport, report to the nearest MACC office and refrain from contacting prosecution witnesses.
Defence counsel Hafiz Norkhan, representing the accused, urged the court to consider a minimum bail of about RM15,000.
“The accused has a wife and three children aged 16, 15 and eight. I was also informed that the accused’s wife has only recently been diagnosed with cerebral palsy.
“The accused also appeared voluntarily in court and has co-operated throughout the investigation,” he said.
The court subsequently set bail at RM20,000 and allowed all the additional conditions, fixing Nov 3 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Tengku Zafrul: Asean’s next integration stage could draw on Malaysia’s NIMP 2030 principles
Article:
SINGAPORE, Sept 21 — Asean’s next stage of economic integration could draw on the principles underpinned by Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
He said NIMP 2030, which was launched in 2023, became a key industrial pillar of the broader Madani Economy framework by aiming to advance economic complexity, accelerate tech adoption, push for net zero, as well as safeguarding economic security and inclusivity.
Tengku Zafrul noted that Asean sits strategically between the East and West, astride some of the world’s most important trading routes.
“We have large consumer markets, abundant resources, growing digital economies and diverse pools of talent.
“Asean received US$226 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in foreign direct investment in 2024, almost twice the  level recorded in 2015. The key question is what that investment brings to our people,” he said in his keynote address titled “Beyond Profit: Closing the Wealth Gap as Asean and China’s Greatest Competitive Advantage” at the 2026 China-Asean Business Leaders Summit on Monday.
Meanwhile, he emphasised that manufacturing and industrial development remain crucial to the region as their impact extends across suppliers, logistics, professional services, technology, energy and skills.
“Done right, an investment leaves a legacy of know-how, stronger firms and better-skilled workers. That same principle should guide Asean’s next stage of development,” he added.
Tengku Zafrul highlighted that Asean and China both carry indigenous traditions that already treat shared prosperity as a condition of good business.
According to him, the lesson for Asean and China in the current global landscape is that closing the wealth gap requires the same policy intent that built the growth in the first place.
Both economies have different strengths, different levels of development and different pools of talent, he noted, stressing that regional integration should allow those strengths to reinforce one another while giving companies a larger market and room to grow.
“A stronger regional economy also creates more opportunities for people and businesses to build wealth,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Did someone just win a ‘H1’ plate with a RM10.7m bid? RTD keeps everyone guessing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A bid of RM10.7 million for the coveted H1 vehicle registration number has raised eyebrows online after bidding for the special H series closed yesterday, although the Road Transport Department (RTD) has yet to confirm the figure.
The amount began circulating on social media yesterday, with several posts showing three different bids for H1 — RM10.7 million, RM666,666 and RM555,777.
According to
Berita Harian
, RTD is expected to announce the official results today, with bidders to be notified through email and their JPJeBid accounts within 24 hours of the bidding closing, subject to bank transaction processing.
The H series, covering H1 to H9999, was open for bidding from September 16 to 20 and is the final single-letter prefix series to be offered by RTD and the government.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli, who launched the series on September 14 in conjunction with Malaysia Day, previously said the letter H represents “harmony” and encouraged the public to bid for the numbers.
Before the H series, the highest confirmed the bid was RM1.75 million for FFF 1, won by King of Malaysia Sultan Ibrahim in June 2024 and the highest amount ever paid for a Malaysian vehicle registration number.
An unconfirmed screenshot shows an online bid for the ‘H1’ vehicle plate for RM10.777 million, possibly a new record for the highest JPJ number plate bid in Malaysia. — Picture from Facebook/J Empire Car Plate
So if RTD confirms the H1 result at RM10.777 million, it would be more than six times the amount paid in 2024.
The JPJeBid system — RTD’s online auction platform for vehicle registration numbers — has no maximum bid limit, allowing bidders to offer large sums for registration numbers they consider exclusive or personally significant.
However, only the official JPJeBid result will determine the winning bid, meaning figures displayed during the bidding process or shared on social media may not reflect the final price.

Title: Socso confirms Ipoh crash victims’ families entitled to pensions and funeral aid exceeding RM275,000
Article:
IPOH, Sept 21 — The next of kin of two victims killed in a road crash on Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here on Saturday are eligible for benefits under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam Scheme for Non-Occupational Accidents.
Perkeso said in a statement today that the victims were Muhammad Izdihar Rafiq Sarajil Korin and Muhamad Faiz Danial Jumri, both aged 19.
Its records showed that Muhammad Izdihar began contributing to Perkeso after starting work in January this year, while Muhamad Faiz had been contributing since August last year.
“Although the accident occurred outside working hours, the next of kin, including the victims’ parents and siblings who may previously have depended on them, remain protected.
“This is the true purpose of Lindung 24 Jam, which provides protection for accidents occurring outside working hours, even when workers have only recently started contributing to Perkeso,” the statement said.
According to Perkeso, the next of kin of Muhammad Izdihar are eligible for Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM945, distributed according to their respective shares, with his parents receiving the payments for life and his three siblings receiving them until they turn 21 or complete a degree.
For Muhamad Faiz, Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM891, distributed according to the respective shares, will be paid to his parents for life, while one sibling will receive the benefit until turning 21 or completing a degree.
In addition, the next of kin of both victims are eligible for a Funeral Management Benefit of RM3,000 each as a one-off payment.
Perkeso said the total periodic pension payments through the Dependants’ Benefit over 15 years to the victims’ next of kin would amount to more than RM275,000.
The crash, which occurred at about 3.35am on Sept 19, killed three male motorcyclists aged between 19 and 20 at the scene, while nine other male motorcyclists aged between 19 and 25 sustained various injuries. — Bernama

Title: Rauf: BN open to alliances for Melaka polls, but don’t negotiate on social media
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 21 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has advised parties interested in collaborating with the coalition in the upcoming state election not to negotiate such matters via social media.
He said doing so could create a negative public perception of the parties involved.
“I will answer briefly. There is no need for us to negotiate through social media. We will issue official letters to all parties, inviting them to submit proposals on how they could become BN’s best strategic partner. These proposals will then be presented at all levels for a decision,” he said.
Ab Rauf said BN respected all parties interested in working with the coalition, but stressed that any collaboration would ultimately be determined through formal discussions, which would be held later at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTC KL).
He told reporters this after officiating the 2026 National-level National Environment Day celebration here today.
Also present were Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, his deputy Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, and Melaka State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh.
Ab Rauf said BN remained open to negotiations with any party concerning the Melaka state election.
“We are neither closing the door completely nor opening it wide for negotiations,” he said.
In the last state election, BN, led by Ab Rauf, formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 State Legislative Assembly seats. PH won five seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured two.
The term of the current Melaka State Legislative Assembly expires on Dec 30. — Bernama

Title: Kulim man charged with murder after allegedly killing wife in fit of jealousy
Article:
KULIM, Sept 21 — A former technician was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with murdering his wife at their home in Taman Tiram last week.
G. Vikneswaran, 43, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Nur Hamizah Mat Shah, but no plea was recorded as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
He was charged with murdering S. Sila, 39, at a house in Taman Tiram here between 6.30 pm and 9.04 pm on Sept 14.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor S. Preeyaa prosecuted, while Vikneswaran was unrepresented. The court fixed Dec 8 for mention.
The media previously reported that the woman died after allegedly being stabbed 13 times by her husband at their home here.
Kulim district police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring was reported as saying preliminary investigations found that jealousy was suspected to have been the motive, while the suspect later surrendered himself at the Lunas police station. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB says Yamtuan can’t dismiss excos without his advice, insists current line-up still valid
Article:
KUALA LUMPURT, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today that the state's executive councillors remain in office, arguing that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar cannot remove them without his advice.
In a statement a day after the palace announced it had revoked all exco appointments, Ismail said the state's administrative system rests on constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy.
“Based on Part Two of the UUTKNS 1959, the sovereign power of the Ruler in matters of state administration shall be exercised on the advice of the YAB Menteri Besar and the State Executive Council,” he said, citing Article 40(1) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS).
He argued that the Ruler's discretionary powers are limited to matters expressly listed in writing under Article 40(2), and that the power to dismiss or end an exco member's tenure unilaterally is not among them.
Ismail also said Article 38(5), which deals with the tenure of exco members, cannot be read on its own. It must be read with Articles 38(4) and 40(1), he said, meaning any termination or change to the exco line-up during an ongoing administration can only take effect on the MB’s advice or formal request.
He said any dismissal made without such advice would be a legal error, unconstitutional and without force of law.
Ismail said he had never been consulted or advised on the dismissal of any exco member under Article 38(5).
"There is no need to submit a new exco list," he said in effect, as the current councillors remain valid and will continue their duties as usual.
The statement did not directly mention the palace's announcement, but appears to respond to it.
In a statement on Sunday night, Istana Besar Seri Menanti said Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had revoked the exco appointments with immediate effect for breaching their oath of office through their actions and statements on Sept 15.
The palace said exco members hold office at the Ruler's pleasure under Article XXXVIII(5) of the state constitution. It said each affected member had been informed in writing, and it directed Ismail to submit a list of candidates for a new exco under Article XXXVIII(2).
The Sept 15 meeting was where the state exco unanimously decided on an Instrument of Proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz's removal, according to Ismail, and instructed the state secretary to proceed with gazetting it.
The dispute over Tuanku Muhriz's position has drawn in several bodies.
On Sept 17, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang said he remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar, that there is no vacancy, and that the state exco and government have no jurisdiction to decide on the proclamation's validity.
The Attorney General's Chambers later said the April 19 proclamation was invalid for failing to comply with Article 10 of the state constitution. It also said there was no evidence of any ground for disqualification under Article 10(1), and that the MB and exco cannot unilaterally remove the Ruler or declare the office vacant. The AGC noted the matter is before the High Court in Seremban, where an interlocutory injunction remains in force.
Today, Ismail ended his statement by saying the state government would continue to uphold the supremacy of the constitution to ensure administrative stability and preserve the people's mandate.

Title: Ex‑TH Properties deputy GM pleads not guilty to abetting RM14,000 CBT case
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 21 — A former TH Properties deputy general manager of construction projects pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to abetting a criminal breach of trust involving RM14,000 in penalty funds collected from a contractor for a commercial building project owned by Tabung Haji (TH).
Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, is charged with abetting Mohamad Hashim Mukhatap, then a construction manager at THP Timur Sdn Bhd and an agent entrusted with the funds.
The money was allegedly connected to penalties collected from contractor Kelpile Sdn Bhd for a proposed Tabung Haji-owned commercial development on Lot 273, Section 12, Bandar Kota Bharu, Kelantan.
The project involved a 22-storey commercial building comprising 244 serviced apartment units, four penthouses, public amenities, commercial space, parking facilities, a single-level sub-basement and related facilities.
The charge was framed under Section 109, read together with Section 409 of the Penal Code, which provides a maximum prison sentence of 20 years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
On Sept 15, Mohamad Hashim, 53, was charged with criminal breach of trust for allegedly misappropriating the RM14,000 by depositing the funds into his personal bank account.
The offence was allegedly committed between Nov 15, 2017, and Aug 8, 2018, at Sofea Residensi, Lot 10015, Section 12, in the Kota Bharu district.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Asmah Che Wan had proposed bail of RM15,000, while lawyer Fahmi Abd Moin Khairuddin, representing Tengku Kamarolhisham, requested RM5,000.
Fahmi said his client earned RM5,000 a month and had six children, some of whom had recently started working while others were studying at public institutions of higher learning or secondary school.
He also told the court that Tengku Kamarolhisham suffered from several health conditions, including diabetes, heart disease, high blood pressure and high cholesterol. The accused had also been charged in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court with abetting CBT involving a separate project.
Judge Dazuki Ali then set bail at RM8,000 with one surety and ordered the accused to surrender his passport to the court, refrain from interfering with witnesses, and report to the Shah Alam MACC office monthly.
The court set Oct 19 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Police: Preliminary probe finds Ipoh motorcyclists speeding in convoy before fatal crash
Article:
TANJONG MALIM, Sept 21 — Police said preliminary investigations found that the group of motorcyclists involved in the accident along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang, Ipoh, which claimed three lives last Saturday, were believed to have been travelling at high speed while riding in a convoy.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said investigations also found that some members of the group travelling from Ipoh subsequently lost control and crashed into a Toyota Vios.
“Following the collision, the second group of motorcyclists failed to avoid the motorcycles and car that had already been involved in the accident in time and crashed into them,” he told a press conference here today.
Mohd Alwi said the route had also been identified as a hotspot for illegal street racing and road hooliganism, with police conducting operations in the early hours of the morning to curb such activities.
However, he said after police completed their operations at around 3am, the motorcyclists would return to gather and resume the activities.
He added that all parties involved had been identified, and police were still conducting further investigations to determine the actual cause of the accident, including confirming the actual owners of the vehicles involved.
Police had also recorded statements from the motorcyclists involved and the driver of the car involved, except for one victim who is still receiving treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).
He said the 19-year-old male victim from Perak was still receiving treatment at the ICU of Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB), Ipoh, and his statement had yet to be recorded.
The accident, which occurred at about 3.35am on Sept 19, resulted in three male motorcyclists, aged between 19 and 20, killed at the scene, while nine other male motorcyclists, aged between 19 and 25, sustained various injuries.
Meanwhile, Mohd Alwi said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Ipoh district police headquarters (IPD) had conducted 64 operations to curb illegal road racing from January to September 19.
“During the same period, 11 arrests were made under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, while action was taken in 41 vehicle seizure cases under Section 64(1) of the same Act,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Lubok Antu and Kanowit schools close as haze pushes API past 200
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 21 — All primary and secondary schools under the Lubok Antu and Kanowit District Education Offices (PPD) have been ordered to close temporarily with immediate effect due to worsening haze.
The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the decision was made based on Air Pollutant Index (API) readings recorded in the two areas as of 9am today.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s API Status for Sarawak, Kanowit and Lubok Antu had recorded ‘very unhealthy’ API readings of 212 and 207 as of 10am.
“Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) will be implemented during the closure in accordance with the Ministry of Education’s Circular Letter No. 8 of 2016 on the management of teaching and learning during disasters,” the department said in a statement.
It also said that for schools located near districts recording API readings above 200, headmasters and principals may consider implementing PdPR, taking into account the health and safety of pupils.
“Should the API trend show an improvement, with readings falling below 200, headmasters and principals may take action to prepare for the reopening of schools.”
JPNS reminded schools to comply with existing standard operating procedures and guidelines under the Ministry of Education Circular Letter No. 1 of 2019 concerning the health and safety of pupils in schools located in areas affected by critical haze.
It also advised all educational institutions under its purview to comply with guidelines on outdoor activities during hot weather and monitor API readings through the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal.
Education institutions were also urged to follow recommendations issued by the Ministry of Health from time to time to safeguard the health of pupils and education personnel. — The Borneo Post

Title: Amirudin: PH Plus in Melaka more electoral pact than coalition given short preparation window
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 21 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) views the PH Plus cooperation for the Melaka state election as more suitable as an electoral understanding rather than a new political coalition, given the increasingly limited time for preparations.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the time available was currently too short to form a new coalition, but an understanding for electoral purposes could still be reached.
“I think it would not be a coalition, but perhaps a political understanding. More towards an electoral understanding.
“With the limited time available, it is too short to form a coalition. But if it is an electoral understanding, it can still be done,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of the Masjid Tanah PKR election machinery in Kuala Sungai Baru here last night.
Also present were the Prime Minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin and acting Melaka PKR State Leadership Council (MPN) chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim.
The Selangor Menteri Besar said discussions on the matter were still at the state level, and that he needed to obtain further details on the outcome of the negotiations before the matter could be referred to the PH leadership at the central level.
He said that if the outcome of the discussions was in line with PH’s needs and met the current requirements, PH would consider implementing the form of cooperation.
Meanwhile, PH also wants Barisan Nasional (BN) to clarify its position on the possibility of cooperation, following the lack of any development on a meeting between the two coalitions so far.
Amirudin said PH had no problem if BN was not interested, but wanted its position to be made known so that PH could make preparations for the upcoming Melaka state election.
“So far, there has been no indication of cooperation, even as we approach the dissolution of the state legislative assembly. Perhaps they are also not interested. So, there is no problem (if they are not interested); we will just proceed (without BN),” he said.
He also said PH was prepared for various scenarios, including contesting on its own, forming a new alignment or cooperating with Umno/BN.
“Whatever happens, as I have said, we are preparing for all scenarios. But PH will not simply wait for developments in the negotiations,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar appeals for unity, tells parties to stop playing racial card when desperate
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has once again cautioned political parties against exploiting racial issues to gain public support.
He said such tactics are often deployed when political parties find themselves in desperate situations, particularly during political dynamics that work against them.
“When politics becomes convoluted and contentious, parties withdraw support and resort to playing the racial card. When desperate, they use race again,” he said when officiating the 41st Malaysia Chinese Cultural Festival at Kota Syahbandar here yesterday.
Also present were Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong and Melaka State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh.
Anwar noted that Malaysia has been independent for 69 years, adding that racial issues should no longer be the primary focus of any community in the country.
As the nation approaches nearly 70 years of independence, Anwar said Malaysia must emerge as a nation that thrives on the collective strength of its diverse races, regardless of who leads the country.
“My speech tonight is more of an appeal – an appeal for us to return to our collective strength. Every voice counts for our survival. Have we not had enough of endless arguments and disputes? Whose country is this? It is our country.
“In the 1940s and 1950s, I can understand. The nation was on the verge of independence, and each group was concerned about its racial survival. In the 1960s, yes, Malaysia was a young nation,” he said.
Anwar stressed that every voice must now focus on the future survival of Malaysia as a unified nation.
“Whoever is given the mandate, whoever is supported, must promise to protect the people, safeguard the country, and secure the future of our children as one nation,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar reiterated that the government will not compromise on corruption and abuse of power, pledging to eradicate it completely.
“My government and I will show zero tolerance, and I will continue to act decisively to clean this country of corruption,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two Negeri Sembilan excos confirm getting palace dismissal letter
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan State Executive Councillor Suhaimizan Bizar has confirmed receiving a formal letter revoking his appointment with immediate effect last night.
Suhaimizan, who is the Gemencheh assemblyman and held the Health, Unity, Information, National Integration and Non-Governmental Organisations portfolio, declined to comment further on the circumstances surrounding the dismissal,
Sinar Harian
reported.
“I did receive the letter last night via WhatsApp. But I cannot comment. Sorry.
“I’m also not sure who sent it, I think it was from the Palace.”
Bernama
reported separately that State Entrepreneurship, Human Resources, Climate Change, Cooperatives and Consumerism Committee chairman Fairuz also confirmed receiving his dismissal letter from the state palace.
Efforts to contact other affected state executive councillors to ascertain further developments were unsuccessful.
The termination follows a royal decree by Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, who stripped the state’s executive councillors of their posts with immediate effect, stating that they breached their oaths of office through actions and statements made on September 15.
In a statement last night, Istana Besar Seri Menanti noted that under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959, members of the State Executive Council hold office at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The palace noted that all council members had taken and signed their oaths and pledges of allegiance before Tuanku Muhriz on August 7, prior to their official appointments.
Under that oath, councillors pledged allegiance to the Ruler and the royal institution, undertook to defend and preserve the state constitution, and recognized the authority vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
The royal rebuke stems from the September 15 meeting where the state executive council unanimously resolved to endorse an Instrument of Proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz’s purported removal from the throne, instructing the state secretary to proceed with its official gazettement.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim confirmed that the state administration had collectively determined the proclamation to be valid.
